tieBreakers.name: The most specific business object wins
tieBreakers.rule: Match the task against the object list in order (specialty apps, then subledgers, then the General Ledger, then Company/Reports services). The first hit decides the application: a job beats an invoice, an invoice beats an account, any business object beats a platform service.

tieBreakers.name: Transaction approvals go to the Approval Workbench
tieBreakers.rule: Approving, declining or routing a transaction (invoice, payment, PO, journal entry) happens in Company › All › Approvals › Approval Workbench. Approving a non-transaction record (vendor record, bank rec, work paper, expense report, timesheet/PTO) stays in that record's own application.

tieBreakers.name: Bulk loads and conversions go to Import Data
tieBreakers.rule: Loading records from a template (master lists, opening balances, history, open items) happens in Company › All › Import Data. An import button on one working list (a budget, a bank feed/BAI file, a funds-transfer or payment file, staff expenses) stays on that list.
tieBreakers.unless: \b(budgets?|bank feeds?|bai|csv or bai|bank statements?|funds transfers?|payments?|expenses|segment rules?|catalog|draws?|draw models?|cost codes?|transaction allocations?|investor data|summary|working budgets?|pex|prepaids?|account groups?|account group members|reporting accounts?)\b

tieBreakers.name: Money direction decides AP vs AR vs Cash
tieBreakers.rule: Money leaving to anyone (vendors, resident deposit refunds, owner payouts by check) is an A/P payment. Money arriving against a customer charge is an A/R payment/deposit. Money arriving with no customer charge, or moving between your own bank accounts, is Cash Management (Other Receipts / Funds Transfer).

tieBreakers.name: Groups and structures are reporting setup
tieBreakers.rule: Customer / location / vendor groups and dimension structures are maintained in Reports › Setup (Dimension Groups / Structures), not in the application that owns the records.

tieBreakers.name: Balance-sheet account reports belong to Financial Close
tieBreakers.rule: A report named after a balance-sheet account (Prepaid Expenses, Accrued Expenses, Notes Payable, A/R - Multifamily, Security Deposits …) is a close work-paper report in Financial Close Management › All › Reports.

tieBreakers.name: "Create X from Y": the Y list hosts the action
tieBreakers.rule: When a task starts from an existing record ("create a PO from a contract", "an intercompany bill from an A/P invoice", "a journal entry from the workbench"), go to the source record's list.

tieBreakers.name: Moving money between your own accounts is a funds transfer
tieBreakers.rule: Moving cash between two of your own bank accounts (operating to reserve, sweep to trust) is Cash Management › Periodic Tasks › Funds Transfer, even when one account is a reserve or escrow account.

tieBreakers.name: A period-end process beats the document it is about
tieBreakers.rule: When the verb is a period-end process (accrue, amortize a prepaid, allocate), the General Ledger process list wins over the invoice or bill it concerns: accruals, prepaids and allocations are worked in General Ledger › All › Periodic Tasks.

exceptionGroups.company: Lives in Company, not in its functional application
exceptionGroups.reports: Lives in Reports / a reporting layer, not in the application's own menu

exceptions.title: Transaction approvals and budget checks
exceptions.trap: You look for invoice, payment, PO or journal-entry approvals (and the "available budget" check) inside AP, Spend or GL.
exceptions.why: Approval routing is one engine shared by every transaction type, so it is configured and worked once, in Company.
exceptions.hook: Anything waiting for a signature sits on one desk: Company › Approvals.

exceptions.title: Bulk imports and opening balances
exceptions.trap: You look for "import vendors / A/P invoices / journal entries / bank rec items" in the owning application.
exceptions.why: Conversions and go-live loads use one template engine (Import Data) so every file is validated the same way.
exceptions.hook: Moving in? The loading dock is in Company.

exceptions.title: Central Configuration tabs for AP, AR, Cash and Site View
exceptions.trap: You open Accounts Payable › Setup › Configuration to change payment priority, inline credits or A/R formatting across entities.
exceptions.why: Multi-entity companies set cross-entity defaults once in Company; each application's Setup › Configuration holds only its own local switches.
exceptions.hook: Local switch = app Setup; company-wide switch = Central Configuration.

exceptions.title: App-specific permissions and user flags
exceptions.trap: You look for "BVA user", chart-type permission or expense-report approver settings in GL or AP.
exceptions.why: A permission is a property of the user, and users live in Company.
exceptions.hook: If it is about a person, it is in Company › Setup › Users/Roles.

exceptions.title: Subscription switches (vendor restrictions, 1099 by tax ID, multi-entity, full service)
exceptions.trap: You look for "enable vendor restrictions" or "validate 1099 by tax ID" in AP Setup.
exceptions.why: Features that change how an application is licensed or shared across entities are turned on from the subscription, in Company.
exceptions.hook: Turning a whole feature on? Subscriptions, in Company.

exceptions.title: Customer Utility Tool (mass inactivate vendors, change default bank G/L)
exceptions.trap: You try to inactivate stale vendors or change a bank account's G/L from the vendor or bank list.
exceptions.why: Bulk data-maintenance utilities run outside the normal record lists.
exceptions.hook: Mass clean-up = Company utility, not the list.

exceptions.title: Tax codes and contact tax groups
exceptions.name: \btax\b
exceptions.trap: You expect tax codes under Accounts Receivable › Setup › Tax.
exceptions.why: Tax codes are shared by A/P, A/R and Spend lines, so the code list is a company setting; A/R Setup keeps the authorities and schedules.
exceptions.hook: Code in Company, authority in A/R.

exceptions.title: Close Calendar generates close work and posts depreciation
exceptions.trap: You look for "generate FCM checklists", "open BVA periods" or "post depreciation for fixed assets" in FCM, GL or Fixed Assets.
exceptions.why: The Close Calendar is the company-wide scheduler that triggers period tasks in several applications.
exceptions.hook: Scheduled month-end triggers hang on the Company calendar.

exceptions.title: Entity record settings (default bank, vendor/customer link, posting date)
exceptions.trap: You look for an entity's default bank account or its linked vendor/customer in Cash, AP or AR.
exceptions.why: The entity (property) record owns its defaults; applications read them.
exceptions.hook: Property-level defaults live on the entity card.

exceptions.title: Contract-expiration and other Ledger Sentry alerts
exceptions.trap: You look for contract-expiration alerts under AP › Bids and Contracts.
exceptions.why: Ledger Sentry is the company-wide rules/alert engine.
exceptions.hook: Alerts = Ledger Sentry.

exceptions.title: AI configuration
exceptions.where: ^(Company › All › - › AI Configuration|Finance Agent › Setup › - › AI Configuration)
exceptions.trap: You look for AI-invoice scanning or standard vendor types in AP Setup.
exceptions.why: AI features are configured once for the agent that serves several applications.
exceptions.hook: AI knobs: Company › AI Configuration / Finance Agent › Setup.

exceptions.title: Named financial statements (Income Statement, Balance Sheet, budget comparisons)
exceptions.trap: You look for the Income Statement or Annual Budget Statement under General Ledger › Reports.
exceptions.why: Statements are Financial Report Writer layouts, so they live in the report library shared by all applications; GL keeps Trial Balance and analytics.
exceptions.hook: Trial balance in GL; the statements you hand an owner in Reports.

exceptions.title: Locations, departments and groups maintained as dimensions
exceptions.trap: You look for location groups, customer groups or the department list in Company or AR.
exceptions.why: Grouping exists for reporting roll-ups, so the Reports application owns dimension groups and structures.
exceptions.hook: If it only exists to roll up a report, it is in Reports › Setup.

exceptions.title: Stored, scheduled and exported report output
exceptions.where: ^(Reports › Setup › (-|More) › (My Stored Reports|Report)|Reports › All › - › Reports Center)
exceptions.name: \b(stor(e|ing|ed)|schedul|cloud|portal|export|email)
exceptions.trap: You look for where a stored or scheduled report went inside the application that ran it.
exceptions.why: Every application hands output to the same Process & Store service.
exceptions.hook: Output goes to one shelf: My Stored Reports.

exceptions.title: OneSite resident reports (rent roll, deposits, resident balances)
exceptions.where: ^(Reports › All › - › Reports Center|General Ledger › All › Reports › Financial Statements)
exceptions.name: \b(rent roll|security deposits?|resident|bank deposit|lost rent|units? report|onesite)
exceptions.trap: You look for the rent roll or resident deposit audit in Accounts Receivable.
exceptions.why: Resident ledgers live in OneSite (property management); Financial Suite only reports them through Reports Center › OneSite Reports.
exceptions.hook: Residents are OneSite's; you only read them in Reports Center.

exceptions.title: Custom report builder in Platform Services (incl. Positive Pay files)
exceptions.where: ^(Platform Services › All › - › Custom Reports|Reports › All › - › (Operational Reports|Custom Reports))
exceptions.trap: You look for the Custom Report Wizard or the Positive Pay report under Reports or Cash Management.
exceptions.why: Custom reports are built on the customization platform, so the wizard lives with object customization.
exceptions.hook: Build-your-own report = Platform Services.

exceptions.title: "Document Dashboard" is AP's scanning queue
exceptions.trap: The name sends you to the Dashboards application.
exceptions.why: It is the inbox of scanned invoice documents before they become A/P invoices.
exceptions.hook: Documents waiting to become invoices = AP.

exceptions.title: Customer refunds start in AR, are paid through AP
exceptions.where: ^(Accounts Receivable › All › (Daily Tasks › Receive a Payment|Search & Find › Payments)|Accounts Payable › All › (Search & Find › Payments|Daily Tasks › Third Party Payments Queue|- › Third Party Payments Queue))
exceptions.name: \b(refund|credit to an invoice|writing off|reversing a paid invoice|applying)
exceptions.trap: A resident/customer refund: AR or AP?
exceptions.why: The credit balance is cleared on the customer (AR › Receive a Payment › Refunding a Customer); the cash leaves as an A/P payment (check, virtual refund or third-party queue).
exceptions.hook: Decide it in AR, pay it in AP.

exceptions.title: Bank reconciliation: Cash does it, FCM files it, Finance Agent can pre-approve it
exceptions.where: ^(Finance Agent › All › - › Cash Management|Financial Close Management › All › Reports › Cash)
exceptions.trap: You look for the bank rec in General Ledger, or for the AI's pending recs in Cash Management.
exceptions.why: Matching and approval happen in Cash › Periodic Tasks › Reconciliation; the close work paper (Cash & Cash Equivalents) is an FCM report; AI-prepared recs queue in Finance Agent.
exceptions.hook: Match in Cash, file in FCM, let the Agent queue.

exceptions.title: Capital projects: PO/contract → A/P invoice → job draw → fixed asset
exceptions.where: ^(Job Cost & Reserves › All › (Search & Find › Subcontracts|Periodic Tasks › Budgets)|Accounts Payable › All › - › (Subcontracts|Purchase Orders|Assets)|Accounts Payable › All › Periodic Tasks › Assets)
exceptions.trap: A construction invoice with retainage: Spend, AP or Job Cost?
exceptions.why: The commitment starts in Spend/AP Bids and Contracts, the invoice is an A/P invoice coded to a job and cost code, draws and retainage are tracked in Job Cost, and the finished asset is created from AP then activated in Fixed Assets.
exceptions.hook: Commit in Spend, bill in AP, draw in Job Cost, capitalize in Fixed Assets.

exceptions.title: Contracts are an AP periodic task; POs made from them are too
exceptions.where: ^Accounts Payable › All › Periodic Tasks › Bids and Contracts
exceptions.trap: "Create a PO / subcontract / service contract from a contract" sends you to Spend Management.
exceptions.why: Bids and Contracts is the A/P contract register; the PO it spawns then lives in Spend.
exceptions.hook: The contract is AP's; the PO it spawns is Spend's.

exceptions.title: Check stock, alignment and ACH set-up help sit in AP Banking
exceptions.name: \b(stock|alignment|electronic payments|ach|signature|printer)
exceptions.trap: Bank-facing check settings sound like Cash Management.
exceptions.why: AP Banking is where checks are printed, so the printing prerequisites are documented there; the bank's check layout itself is Cash › Setup › More.
exceptions.hook: Printing problems: AP Banking. Layout design: Cash Setup.

exceptions.title: Vendor e-payment enrollment is on the vendor, not in Cash
exceptions.name: \b(electronic payments?|ach|eft)\b
exceptions.trap: "Set up vendors for ACH" sounds like a bank configuration.
exceptions.why: The remittance method and bank details are fields on the vendor record; Cash only holds your side of the file.
exceptions.hook: Their bank details = vendor record; your bank file = Cash.

exceptions.title: Four kinds of budget
exceptions.where: ^(Forecasting & Planning › All › (- › Budgets|Periodic Tasks › Working Budgets)|Job Cost & Reserves › All › (Periodic Tasks › Budgets|Search & Find › Jobs))
exceptions.name: \bbudget
exceptions.trap: Every "budget" task goes to General Ledger › Budgets.
exceptions.why: GL holds the posted operating budget and BVA; Forecasting & Planning builds working budgets before publishing; Job Cost holds job and change-order budgets; Company approvals check available budget.
exceptions.hook: Operating = GL, draft = F&P, capital = Job Cost, spending check = Company.

exceptions.title: Opening and closing books from FCM Console
exceptions.name: \b(open|close) books\b
exceptions.trap: Books open/close is a GL month-end task.
exceptions.why: It is (GL › Periodic Tasks › Month End › Books), but FCM's Console exposes the same Open/Close Books boxes for the close team.
exceptions.hook: Same switch, two panels: GL Month End and FCM Console.

exceptions.title: Account labels are kept per subledger
exceptions.trap: Labels map to G/L accounts, so you look in General Ledger.
exceptions.why: A label is the subledger's friendly name for a G/L account; each subledger keeps its own label list.
exceptions.hook: Labels belong to the subledger that uses them.

exceptions.title: Customer types exist in AR and in Cash Management
exceptions.trap: Customer types must be an A/R setup code.
exceptions.why: Cash Management keeps its own customers and types for credit-card and PC-card billing.
exceptions.hook: Card-program customers belong to Cash.

exceptions.title: Job positions are payroll planning, not Job Cost
exceptions.where: ^(Forecasting & Planning › All › - › Job Positions|Time & Resources › All › Periodic Tasks › Job Positions)
exceptions.trap: "Job" sends you to Job Cost & Reserves.
exceptions.why: A job position is an HR/payroll object (Forecasting & Planning payroll, Time & Resources staffing).
exceptions.hook: A job *position* is a person's role, not a construction job.

exceptions.title: "Agent Jobs" and "Agent Accruals" belong to the Finance Agent
exceptions.trap: "Job" or "accrual" sends you to Job Cost or GL.
exceptions.why: These are the AI agent's scheduled work and proposed accruals, reviewed before anything posts.
exceptions.hook: Agent-prefixed = Finance Agent.

exceptions.title: A/R keeps an "Invoices" list without the A/R prefix
exceptions.where: ^Accounts Receivable › All › (- › (Invoices|A/R Sales Invoices)|Reports › A/R Invoices Analysis|Search & Find › Payments)
exceptions.trap: A bare "invoice" defaults to A/P.
exceptions.why: Inside the A/R menu the sales-invoice list is simply called Invoices.
exceptions.hook: Check which menu you are in before trusting a bare "invoice".

exceptions.title: "Posted Payments" and payment requests are A/P
exceptions.name: \b(posted payments?|payment requests?|notification)
exceptions.trap: "Posted payment" sounds like cash received in A/R.
exceptions.why: Posted Payments is the list of A/P disbursements after the check run.
exceptions.hook: A/P posts payments out; A/R enters payments in.

exceptions.title: Spend Management setup reaches into GL and AP
exceptions.trap: Mapping G/L accounts to catalog categories or the Site View A/P close calendar sounds like GL or AP setup.
exceptions.why: Both only matter to purchasing, so Spend owns them.
exceptions.hook: Only purchasing cares? Spend Setup.

exceptions.title: Multi-currency switches are in GL and AR configuration
exceptions.name: \b(currenc|multi-currency|segments?|foreign)
exceptions.trap: Currency and segment settings sound like Company-wide options.
exceptions.why: Company defines currencies; GL (Accounting Settings) and AR decide how they post and revalue.
exceptions.hook: Define in Company, post-behaviour in GL/AR Setup.

exceptions.title: Voiding a check is done from the Check Register
exceptions.name: \bvoid
exceptions.trap: A register is a report, so you do not expect an action there.
exceptions.why: The Check Register lists every issued payment, so it carries the Void action; voiding restores the invoices to open.
exceptions.hook: Void where the checks are listed: the Check Register.
